title: Keep only the newest ledger payloads in memory; read older ones back from the file, byte-checked
problem: A GREG body keeps every ledger record's payload in memory: 2,639 B of resident memory per retained record measured at #196's head 190c58fb (one holding mission, 60 s cadence). At about 18,700 records a day that is about 49 MB a day, so a 4-8 GB Chromebook body that the founder leaves working for weeks runs out of memory long before disk (FINDING-LEDGER-APPEND-COST-2026-10-14, 'Next measured limit'; option 1 'keep payloads on disk').
baseline: 190c58fb: provenance/ledger.py retains every LedgerRecord with its payload dict; events/spine.py keeps references to every event payload; the Commit Witness reconstructs the whole chain by re-hashing every payload in memory (about 9 us per record).

alternatives.name: Proposed: resident window plus byte-checked reads and a running skeleton digest
alternatives.description: File-backed ledgers keep payloads of genesis and the newest RESIDENT_RECORDS (1,024) records; older payloads are re-read with pread and refused unless the bytes' SHA-256 equals the digest bound when they were written or verified; a running SHA-256 over dropped skeletons replaces payload re-hashing on the commit path; explicit verify_chain also re-reads every dropped line; the spine keeps positions.
advantages: Resident memory per record 2,639 -> 1,458 B; heap 2,270 -> 833 B
Commit-path reconstruction cost drops from O(n x 9 us) to O(window x 9 us + n x ~1 us); the measured run was faster
File format, hashes and every read API unchanged
On-disk changes after open become detectable at read time
disadvantages: A dropped payload costs a file read and parse per read
More code in the evidence plane
Memory still grows about 1.4 KB per record
alternatives.revival_evidence: Retained; revisit if a whole-file replay hot path dominates tick time on founder hardware.

alternatives.name: Literal option 1: payloads on disk, full re-hash from disk at every reconstruction
alternatives.description: The earlier finding's wording: memory holds hashes and offsets; verification still reads everything, now from disk.
disadvantages: Measured 2x slower body (690 s vs 352 s for 1,800 ticks): the Commit Witness re-read and re-parsed every dropped line at every Gate commit
alternatives.revival_evidence: Only if Commit Witness reconstruction moves off the per-observation path (a Gate change, founder decision).

alternatives.name: Option 2: checkpoint and archive segments
alternatives.description: Anchor the head, seal verified history into segment files, keep only the open segment and signed projection checkpoints in memory.
advantages: The only route to memory that does not grow with history
disadvantages: Projections over old segments (mission book, spine views, Gate and passport registries) need signed checkpoints; changes evidence-plane and governance semantics
alternatives.revival_evidence: Founder decision on checkpoint semantics; the remaining growth after this change (skeleton 500 B, Gate 120 B, passports 40 B per record) is the measured input.

alternatives.name: Option 3: fewer records per read-only observation
alternatives.description: A lighter Gate path for read-only sensors (13 records per observation today).
advantages: Cuts every per-record cost at once
disadvantages: Changes governance of observations; not an engineering call
alternatives.revival_evidence: Founder ruling on read-only observation governance.

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: A body observing once a minute grows about 49 MB a day and exhausts a Chromebook's memory in weeks; the founder's persistent-work destination fails on its first body.
advantages: No change to the evidence plane
disadvantages: Persistent operation measured to fail within weeks on founder hardware
Commit-path reconstruction keeps growing at 9 us per record

roles.position: Persistent work while the founder is away is an active N1 requirement; a body that dies of memory in weeks contradicts it. The change keeps every byte of history and adds no authority.
material_concerns: Must not be presented as bounded memory: growth continues at about 1.4 KB per record
VEPMC is unaffected; founder-device acceptance remains the gate

roles.position: Commodity mechanisms only (pread, SHA-256, OS page cache). No new store, index service or authority plane. One owner (provenance/ledger.py) for retention; the spine reads through it.
material_concerns: Retained records are now of two kinds (resident, dropped); consumers of the private list must not depend on payload identity for old records
The genesis record stays resident by design

roles.position: The integrity guarantees must survive: in-memory alteration found by explicit verification, by the next Commit Witness and by the hot path; nothing appended onto altered history; eviction must not heal an alteration.
material_concerns: The first version failed open: a Commit Witness was appended after a read had found changed bytes on disk

The commit path relies on a running digest the process itself bound; a consistent in-process rewrite of skeleton and digest evades it, as a consistent in-process rewrite of payloads and hashes evaded the old check
Independent review found pointer laundering (F1): explicit verify_chain now re-derives every dropped hash from the file and eviction binds the pointer first
evidence_refs: independent adversarial review recorded in the PR

roles.position: Measured faster and smaller on the same scenario; reversible by reverting one commit with no data migration.
material_concerns: Whole-history replays (settlement) now read old events from the file each tick
A changed file now stops appends until reconciled: correct, but an operator must know how to reopen

roles.position: No evidence is deleted or rewritten; history files are byte-identical; on-disk tampering after open becomes visible sooner. Negative results (2x slowdown, fail-open) are kept.
material_concerns: Claims must stay at UNIT-TESTED and LOCAL measured tier; nothing is founder-device verified

evidence.claim: Resident memory per retained record falls from 2,639 B to 1,458 B on the same body scenario
evidence.finding: Slope from 7,820 to 23,420 records; 1,800 ticks each

evidence.claim: Python heap per record falls from about 2,270 B to 833 B; payloads leave the heap
evidence.finding: decoder.py share falls from 65% to a constant window

evidence.claim: Files are byte-identical and every read API equals a ledger holding everything
evidence.finding: Line-for-line comparison and readout equality on the same file

evidence.claim: Existing ledger, spine, Gate, mission-book and disclosure suites pass unchanged
evidence.reference: tests/unit/test_provenance.py and seven more files (136 tests)
evidence.finding: All pass; their ledgers are smaller than the window

evidence.claim: An independent differential test matches the old ledger and spine exactly
evidence.reference: independent review, test_differential.py (36 random sequences at windows 1-3)

counterevidence.claim: Literal option 1 doubled body run time
counterevidence.finding: 690 s vs 352 s; replaced by the two-level reconstruction
Skeleton about 500 B, Gate grants about 120 B, passports about 40 B per record

counterevidence.claim: The first version failed open after detecting on-disk change
counterevidence.finding: Fixed: every reconstruction reads the file once a read has found a change

counterevidence.claim: Independent adversarial review of 45d65a30 reproduced five breaks: pointer laundering (high), type-only changes (medium), exceptions after fsync (medium), a race erasing the tamper signal (low-medium), shared payload objects (low)
counterevidence.reference: FINDING-BODY-MEMORY-2026-10-28.md, 'Independent adversarial review'; tests/unit/test_ledger_dropped_payloads.py (13 tests fail on 45d65a30)
counterevidence.finding: All five fixed and pinned; a replaced ledger file is now also detected

pass_1.intended_outcome: A body's memory no longer holds every payload of its history, with no change to what is written, what any reader sees, or which alterations are detected.

advantages.statement: Payloads, the largest share of growth, leave memory
advantages.amplified_value: Weeks become months on the first body before memory binds; the page cache serves old reads from reclaimable memory

advantages.statement: The commit path reconstruction gets cheaper
advantages.amplified_value: Per-observation cost no longer re-hashes all history; measured run 33% faster

advantages.statement: On-disk changes after open are detected at read time
advantages.amplified_value: Tampering with the file is refused within the running process, not only at the next restart

disadvantages.statement: Re-reading dropped payloads costs CPU on whole-history replays
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Fast parse of digest-verified bytes; measured end-to-end run faster; the replay hot path is named as the next CPU limit

disadvantages.statement: Commit-path reconstruction no longer re-derives dropped payload hashes
disadvantages.redesigned_response: A running SHA-256 over dropped skeletons and line digests catches any in-memory change; explicit verify_chain re-reads the bytes; any reopening (the appraiser's included) re-derives every hash

disadvantages.statement: An alteration in memory could be healed by eviction
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Only payloads that still hash to their record are dropped, in order; an altered one stays for detection (tested)
Remaining growth measured by component and handed to the owners and decisions that can remove it

comparisons.baseline: Everything in memory: 2,639 B per record, full re-hash per Gate commit
comparisons.do_nothing: Fails the persistent-body requirement within weeks on a Chromebook
comparisons.strongest_competing_architecture: Option 2 segments: only route to non-growing memory but needs founder decisions on checkpoint semantics
comparisons.reversible_experiment: This change: one revert, no migration, byte-identical files; window size is a constructor parameter

rejected_alternatives.name: Literal option 1: re-derive every dropped hash from disk at every reconstruction
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Measured 2x slower body: the Commit Witness re-read and re-parsed every dropped line at every Gate commit (690 s vs 352 s)
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: Commit Witness reconstruction moved off the per-observation path by a founder decision on the Gate

rejected_alternatives.name: Option 3: fewer records per read-only observation
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Changes the governance of observations; not an engineering call
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: A founder ruling on read-only observation governance

rejected_alternatives.name: Compress payloads in memory
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Still grows with history and adds CPU per read; the file already holds the bytes
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: A body without a durable file (none today)

pass_2.attack_summary: Attacked the strengthened design for fail-open paths, healing, consistency of skeleton tampering, performance cliffs, thread and reader races, and overclaiming.

new_weaknesses.statement: After detecting changed bytes on disk, the commit path (which does not read the file) appended a witness
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: _LineSource.broken forces every reconstruction to read the file until it is intact; test added

new_weaknesses.statement: Two kinds of retained record and two reconstruction depths are harder to reason about
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Single owner, documented in the module and FINDING-BODY-MEMORY-2026-10-28; tests name each guarantee

new_weaknesses.statement: The window size 1,024 was chosen on one scenario
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Constructor parameter and module constant; the scenario is the one the earlier finding used; revisit on founder hardware

new_weaknesses.statement: Independent review: a line pointer altered while resident was folded into the running digest at eviction, so forged bytes elsewhere in the file were served and verified
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Eviction requires the pointer to name exactly the record's bytes; explicit verify_chain re-derives each dropped record's hash from the file; records kept past the window have their pointers judged on the commit path

new_weaknesses.statement: Independent review: type-only skeleton changes, post-fsync exceptions, and a race clearing the tamper signal
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Type-strict ascii encoding with exact type checks; all fallible work before the write and uncertain-on-failure after it; failure counters instead of a flag

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Measured end-to-end improvement; replay cost is pre-existing linear growth
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Tick time on founder hardware exceeds the 30 s tick interval or a replay dominates a profile

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Running digest plus explicit re-read plus reopen re-derivation keep every detection path the old code had
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any independent review finding an undetected in-memory alteration

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Eviction checks the hash first; tested
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: A test showing an altered payload dropped

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Remaining growth sits in the Gate (pinned), identity registry and the skeleton; each needs a decision or a larger refactor
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.owner: Founder (Gate, option 2); identity owner (passports); ledger maintainer (skeleton packing)
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Founder decision on the Gate claim scan or option 2

pass_2.final_design: Resident window of 1,024 payloads; byte-checked reads with fast parse; running skeleton digest; explicit verify_chain re-reads every dropped line; commit path and schedule do not read the file unless a read found a change; streaming open; spine keeps positions.

residual_risks.risk: A consistent in-process rewrite of skeleton and running digest is not detected in-process
residual_risks.mitigation: Same class as before (a consistent in-process rewrite of payloads and hashes was not detected either); reopening and the separate-process appraiser re-derive every hash from the file
residual_risks.review_trigger: Any proposal to trust in-process verification as an external proof

residual_risks.risk: Memory still grows about 1.4 KB per record
residual_risks.mitigation: Measured and attributed; option 2 and Gate/passport decisions named

dissent.handling: Recorded with threshold; does not block a draft, blocks adoption if met.

entries.position: The commit path should keep re-deriving every hash from payload bytes, as before, regardless of cost. (Explicit verify_chain now does; the commit path uses the running digest.)
entries.rationale: Re-derivation is independent of any digest this process bound; the running digest is not.
entries.evidence_threshold: A demonstrated in-memory alteration the running digest misses but the old re-hash would have caught
entries.review_trigger: Independent review or mutation testing of _verify_dropped

authority_impact.approver: Alfonso Lopez (adoption into #196 and any merge); #196 integrator for intake

migration_plan: None required: the file format and hashes are unchanged, so existing ledgers open as before and are read back by the new code; reverting restores in-memory retention on the same files.

steps: Revert the commit on the child branch, or decline intake into #196
No data migration: history files are byte-identical either way

kill_criteria: Any read API returns different data than a ledger holding everything in memory
Any in-memory or on-disk alteration the old code detected goes undetected
A record is appended onto history found altered
Body tick time on founder hardware regresses beyond the old code's
decision_owner: Alfonso Lopez decides adoption into the evidence plane (founder decision 5 of HANDOFF-GREG-RECONCILIATION-2026-10-28); the #196 integrator decides intake; session_01Kucyfm6YBHMTjaiC1M9hqD owns the reversible draft. All five roles recommend RETAIN.
review_trigger: Independent review result, founder-device measurement, or a founder decision on option 2 or the Gate
